preamble: Having solved this puzzle, tonight's episode of 'Inside No 9' on BBC2 at 10pm would interest you

clue.text: To wound and wander, destitute

indicators.note: to wander is to stray about, so the letters of the preceding words roam into a new order

explanation.surface: Someone is told to hurt a person and then roam off, left penniless.
explanation.walkthrough: 'wander' looks like a second instruction alongside 'To wound', but it is the anagram signal working on all three words before it.
explanation.definitionFit: An idiom for someone without money, home or prospects; destitute means utterly poor.

clue.text: Indian product of French-Italian agreement

parts.note: de is the French word for of
si is Italian for yes, a word of agreement

explanation.surface: Something from India is presented as the outcome of a Franco-Italian treaty.
explanation.walkthrough: 'product' is a link word: the answer is the product of the two foreign words placed together.
explanation.definitionFit: A South Asian term, used especially in the diaspora, for a person or thing from the Indian subcontinent.

clue.text: Cover sound like a 50 cent song

indicators.note: tells the solver the entry is pronounced the same as the song type that follows

parts.note: 50 Cent is an American rapper, so his kind of song is a rap

explanation.surface: Seems to ask for a cover version that resembles a track by the rapper 50 Cent.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cover' tempts as a cover version of a song; it is the verb or noun for enveloping something.
explanation.definitionFit: To wrap something is to cover it, and a wrap is also a shawl or covering.

clue.text: Why, say, a setter here is disturbed about a Spanish uncle — it's enough to take one's breath away

definitions.text: enough to take one's breath away

indicators.note: about means surrounding, so the jumble goes round the following pieces
disturbed means thrown into disorder, so these letters are jumbled

parts.note: the word why, said aloud, is the letter Y
a sphinx: Sphinx is the pseudonym of the compiler of this puzzle
a plus tio, the Spanish word for uncle

explanation.surface: A rambling joke about the setter in a muddle beside a Spanish relative, ending on something breathtaking.
explanation.walkthrough: Jumbling Y, A and SPHINX gives ASPHYXIN, which goes 'about' A and TIO. The setter, Sphinx, names himself: compilers often refer to themselves in clues.
explanation.definitionFit: Suffocation literally deprives a person of air, so it quite literally stops one breathing.

clue.text: Preliminary drawing of drink from the barrel, say

indicators.note: say signals that the entry is pronounced like the drink described before it

parts.note: beer drawn from a cask is draught beer, a draught

explanation.surface: Sounds like a sketch of someone pouring from a cask.
explanation.walkthrough: In British spelling beer from the barrel is 'draught', which is pronounced exactly like the entry.
explanation.definitionFit: A first rough version or sketch of a drawing or document is called a draft.

clue.text: Knocked back beer and wine, then put on a French undergarment

indicators.note: in this down entry the earlier pieces sit on top of the French article, so it comes first

parts.note: un is the French for a

indicators.note: knocked back suggests drinking, but here it means turned round, reading the words backwards

parts.note: pils is a pilsner-style lager
red is red wine

explanation.surface: Someone downs beer and wine and then dresses in French lingerie.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Knocked back' looks like drinking; it reverses PILS and RED to give DERSLIP.
explanation.definitionFit: A slip worn beneath a dress or skirt is a kind of undergarment.

clue.text: Springs soldiers quietly within

indicators.note: within means the soft marking goes inside the soldiers

parts.note: the SAS is the British Special Air Service regiment
p (piano) is the musical marking for quietly

explanation.surface: Troops creep silently around hot springs.
explanation.definitionFit: Mineral springs, and resorts built around them, are known as spas.

clue.text: Catch a train before poisonous bite

indicators.note: before puts the train ahead of the catch

parts.note: a puffer is a nickname for a steam train
to fish is to try to catch

explanation.surface: Seems to tell you to catch a train before you are bitten by something venomous.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bite' is a mouthful of food: the fish is a famous Japanese delicacy (fugu) that can be deadly if badly prepared.
explanation.definitionFit: This fish contains a deadly toxin, so eating it is a potentially lethal mouthful.

clue.text: Little pot, good for putting on

parts.note: little means short in stature
pot and grass are both slang for cannabis

explanation.surface: Reads like advice that a small amount of cannabis is good for you.
explanation.walkthrough: 'putting on' suggests weight or clothes; it means golf putting, played on a closely mown green.
explanation.definitionFit: Closely cropped turf suits a golf ball rolling on a putting green.

clue.text: Degas evacuated and bathed before putting big picture in bog

definitions.note: a singular word standing for the plural tract of marshy land

indicators.note: in means the overview goes inside, between the two pieces
before sets the swimming ahead of what is left of the painter

parts.note: to swim is to bathe, and swam is its past tense

indicators.note: an evacuated word is emptied of its middle, keeping only the outer letters

parts.note: the big picture is the overall plan

explanation.surface: Suggests the painter Degas, after a swim, hanging a large canvas in a toilet.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bog' tempts as British slang for a toilet, fitting the picture-hanging surface; it means marsh.
explanation.definitionFit: Marshy, waterlogged ground is called bog or swampland, synonyms for wetland.

clue.text: Untangle for a natural hairdo

indicators.note: untangling hair sorts it out, here sorting the two little words into a new order

explanation.surface: Advice to comb out your hair in favour of a natural style.
explanation.definitionFit: A rounded hairstyle of naturally tightly curled hair, worn untreated by straighteners.

clue.text: Could George first digest bananas, before eating good Italian breakfast dish

indicators.note: eating means taking something inside, so the scramble goes round the Italian word
going bananas means going crazy, so these letters are scrambled
first takes the opening letters of the two words before it

parts.note: bene is Italian for good or well

explanation.surface: Asks whether George could stomach bananas before a hearty Italian breakfast.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bananas' is the anagram signal, working on the two first letters plus 'digest'; 'eating' puts that jumble around the Italian word.
explanation.definitionFit: Poached eggs and ham on a muffin with hollandaise sauce, a classic brunch dish.

clue.text: I hear an American poet solved the riddle of the pseudo hotel patron …

parts.note: a riddle is a mystery
Edgar Guest was a popular American poet

explanation.surface: A poet works out the puzzle of a fake guest at a hotel.
explanation.walkthrough: 'I hear' adds a pun: 'Mister E. Guest', the poet's name with title, and 'mystery guessed' (solved the riddle) are both pronounced like the answer. The ellipsis leads into 15-across.
explanation.definitionFit: A secret inspector posing as an ordinary customer to assess the service is a pretend patron.

clue.text: Hawk's equipment has a double catch

definitions.text: Hawk's equipment has a double catch

parts.words: Hawk's equipment has a double catch
parts.note: Tony Hawk is a champion rider of a wheeled plank; a flatfish that might be landed and the verb for getting on a bus are two senses of catch

explanation.surface: A falconer's gear seems to have a fastening with two clips.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Hawk' is not the bird but the skater Tony Hawk, and 'catch' works twice: one fishy, one for transport.
explanation.definitionFit: A wheeled plank ridden by skaters such as Tony Hawk is his sporting gear.

clue.text: Dickens character who undertakes to be a coffin maker

definitions.meaning: the parish undertaker in Oliver Twist

definitions.text: who undertakes to be a coffin maker
definitions.meaning: a pun: one who undertakes, an undertaker, by trade makes coffins

explanation.surface: A Dickensian figure promises to take up the trade of coffin making.
explanation.walkthrough: 'undertakes' looks like 'promises', but points to his trade as an undertaker.
explanation.definitionFit: Mr Sowerberry is the parish undertaker in Oliver Twist, to whom the young orphan is apprenticed.

clue.text: … some smart aleck, no wit allegedly

indicators.note: some means only part of the following words, so the answer is lifted from inside them

explanation.surface: Continuing the previous clue: a smart aleck supposedly lacking any wit.
explanation.walkthrough: The ellipsis links the clue to 12-across but plays no part in the wordplay. 'allegedly' also hints the answer is pronounced like 'no wit all'.
explanation.definitionFit: A conceited person who acts as though they understand everything is a smart aleck.

clue.text: Upset, as pedants often follow cuts

indicators.note: upset means knocked over, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Pedants are annoyed by a sloppy phrase, as they often are after cuts.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cuts' in editing is followed by the familiar phrase 'cuts and pastes', so the answer is what follows it.
explanation.definitionFit: Editing on a computer: one cuts text and then pastes it elsewhere, so the second action follows the first.

clue.text: Hitherto, two notes are joined

parts.note: so and fa are two notes of the sol-fa scale
r is the abbreviation for are, a metric unit of area

explanation.surface: Up to now, a couple of musical notes have been linked.
explanation.definitionFit: A phrase meaning up to the present time, a synonym of until now.

clue.text: Tory leader on board for English flower

indicators.note: on puts the first piece ahead of the next
a leader is the front runner, so only the opening letter of the word is taken

parts.note: board is payment for lodging, that is rent

explanation.surface: A Conservative chief joins a committee in place of an English bloom.
explanation.walkthrough: 'flower' is the crossword trick for something that flows, a river: the Trent runs through the English Midlands.
explanation.definitionFit: Crossword convention reads flower as one that flows, so the river counts as one.

clue.text: Gets and holds down

definitions.meaning: with the shared 'down', gets down means makes someone feel low
presses on something so it stays lowered, like a key or pedal

explanation.walkthrough: 'down' serves both definitions: gets down and holds down.
explanation.definitionFit: The verb covers both lowering someone's mood and physically pushing a button or lever lower.

clue.text: You might at Halloween see Robert on top of slapper, drunk

indicators.note: on top means the name comes first, ahead of the rest

parts.note: Bob is a short form of Robert

indicators.note: drunk means reeling, so the letters stagger into a new order

explanation.surface: A rowdy Halloween party scene with a man named Robert and a drunken woman.
explanation.walkthrough: 'slapper' is British slang for a promiscuous woman; anagrammed with 'of' it gives FORAPPLES.
explanation.definitionFit: A Halloween party game in which players try to grab apples floating in water using only their teeth.

clue.text: Malaysian township, whence traveller returns to capital

indicators.note: returns means goes back, so the word reads backwards

parts.note: a rep is a travelling sales representative
capital means first-rate, A1, written here as AI

explanation.surface: A town in Malaysia from which a traveller heads back to the capital.
explanation.definitionFit: Perai is a town in Penang state, on the Malaysian mainland opposite George Town.

clue.text: Frankfurter's number one bun? Don't start!

indicators.note: don't start means drop the opening letter of each of the two words

explanation.surface: A sausage joke: a frankfurter in a single bun, with an exasperated 'don't start!'
explanation.walkthrough: 'Frankfurter' looks like a hot dog, but means a person from Frankfurt, so a German number is wanted: nine.
explanation.definitionFit: German for nine, the number a native of Frankfurt would say.

clue.text: The Origins of a Species popularised savage serpents

indicators.note: origins are beginnings, so the first letter of each following word is taken

explanation.surface: Echoes Darwin's book title, as if it made fierce snakes popular.
explanation.definitionFit: Asps are small venomous snakes, Cleopatra's legendary choice.

clue.text: Land is endlessly sacred

indicators.note: endlessly means without its ends, so the outer letters are dropped

explanation.surface: A claim that some ground is holy.
explanation.definitionFit: A unit of land area, and in the plural an estate or fields.

clue.text: Strength of support arranged inside unopened truss

indicators.note: arranged means put in order, so the letters are reorganised
unopened means without its opening, dropping the first letter of the word

explanation.surface: Describes an engineer checking how strong a frame is from within a truss.
explanation.walkthrough: NSIDE, from 'inside' 'unopened', is jumbled with TRUSS.
explanation.definitionFit: Robustness, the solidity a good support needs, is its sturdiness.

clue.text: Periods where Fry's sons choose SATS, some say

definitions.text: Periods where Fry's sons choose SATS, some say

parts.words: Periods where Fry's sons choose SATS, some say
parts.note: add the same word to each of Fry, sons, choose and SATS and, pronounced aloud, each turns into a weekday name

explanation.walkthrough: 'some say' asks you to hear the four words as the starts of weekday names: Fri-, Sun-, Tues-, Satur-.
explanation.definitionFit: Periods of twenty-four hours; the week's seven names all end in this same word.

clue.text: Associates fool with first workers

parts.note: an ass is a fool
first is written 1st, with I standing for the figure one
worker ants are the standard crossword workers

explanation.surface: Someone's colleagues are dismissed as a fool and the earliest staff.
explanation.definitionFit: Helpers or aides who work alongside someone, a synonym for associates.
